title: 冲突值得谈吗？用“I”表达邀请一对一沟通
topic: 冲突值得谈吗？用“I”表达邀请一对一沟通

source.title: Resolve a personal conflict - Dropbox Virtual First Communication Kit
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 本课围绕 Dropbox 冲突处理指南的前三步：判断问题是否值得谈，客观整理观察、影响和期望，再用非评判的“I”表达邀请对方一对一沟通。
paragraphs: Not all conflicts are created equal. Before you discuss, try to take a step back. If you’re just a little annoyed, it might be best to let things slide, but if the conflict is truly disruptive, it probably warrants a 1:1 discussion. Use the conflict scorecard below to get better sense. If your conflict feels discussion-worthy, move onto step 2. If you’re not sure, try coming back to it in a day or two. Does it still feel important?

Before you discuss, it’s good to pause and articulate your situation in an objective, honest way. Use the conflict worksheet below to outline what you noticed, how it impacted your work, and what you’d like to have happen instead. This will ground your conversation and help you resolve the conflict more quickly.

When you’re ready to talk, schedule a time that works for you both. Try to do this 1:1 first, before pulling in anyone else. (We like the idea that “feedback should travel the shortest distance between two points”—it’ll help you avoid a drama triangle.) In your invite, see if you can acknowledge the conflict using more “I” statements than “you” statements. Bonus points for a non-judgmental, light tone. For example, “I noticed myself getting flustered in our last meeting. Got time to talk about it?”
translations: 并非所有冲突都一样。讨论前先退一步想想：如果只是有点恼火，最好让它过去；如果冲突确实干扰了工作，可能值得一对一谈谈。可以用冲突评估表帮助判断；若不确定，过一两天再看它是否仍然重要。
讨论前，先停下来，以客观、诚实的方式说明情况。用冲突工作表记下你观察到什么、它怎样影响工作，以及你希望怎样改变。这样能让谈话有事实依据，也有助于更快解决问题。
准备好谈时，安排一个双方都合适的时间。先尝试一对一沟通，再考虑邀请其他人。邀请中尽量多用“I”陈述、少用“You”陈述，以承认冲突，同时保持不评判、轻松的语气。例如：“我发现自己在上次会议中有些慌乱。有时间聊聊吗？”
fullTextParagraphs: Not all conflicts are created equal. Before you discuss, try to take a step back. If you’re just a little annoyed, it might be best to let things slide, but if the conflict is truly disruptive, it probably warrants a 1:1 discussion. Use the conflict scorecard below to get better sense. If your conflict feels discussion-worthy, move onto step 2. If you’re not sure, try coming back to it in a day or two. Does it still feel important?

Before you discuss, it’s good to pause and articulate your situation in an objective, honest way. Use the conflict worksheet below to outline what you noticed, how it impacted your work, and what you’d like to have happen instead. This will ground your conversation and help you resolve the conflict more quickly.

When you’re ready to talk, schedule a time that works for you both. Try to do this 1:1 first, before pulling in anyone else. (We like the idea that “feedback should travel the shortest distance between two points”—it’ll help you avoid a drama triangle.) In your invite, see if you can acknowledge the conflict using more “I” statements than “you” statements. Bonus points for a non-judgmental, light tone. For example, “I noticed myself getting flustered in our last meeting. Got time to talk about it?”

At the start of your meeting, summarize your points from the conflict worksheet above. Then pause while your partner responds. Not everyone has a black belt in conflict resolution, so it’s natural for this part to feel awkward. As you listen, reflect: Did you have different expectations about how things should go? Were you working toward different goals? Were they aware of the behavior you noticed, or was it a “blind spot”? Did you contribute to the conflict in some way?

Sometimes, simply acknowledging a problem diffuses it. Other times, you need a follow-up. Some ideas: If the conflict happened because your roles were unclear, try creating a DACI. If your project has gotten off-track more generally, try a project checkup. Need an outside opinion? Consider escalating your conflict. If the conversation goes sideways or you can’t get to a resolution, take a day to reflect. Would it help to talk with a coach or manager? If you find you’ve contributed to the conflict in some way, remember: the words “I’m sorry” are magic. Extra Credit: Complicate your story. Telling ourselves over-simplified stories about other people’s behavior can have a hugely negative impact on our perceptions and moods. Learning to notice the story we’re telling ourselves—and experiment with alternative ones—can help us get a wiser, more balanced view. Use the Simple story worksheet to get started.
fullTextHeadings: Step 1: Ask yourself, “Is it worth a conversation?”

notes.phrase: if the conflict is truly disruptive, it probably warrants a 1:1 discussion
notes.meaning: 如果冲突确实干扰工作，可能值得一对一讨论
notes.explain: warrant 表示“值得／有必要”；先判断影响程度，不必把每次轻微恼火都升级成正式对话。
notes.example: Repeated handoff changes affect the dashboard, so they may warrant a 1:1 discussion.

notes.phrase: what you noticed, how it impacted your work, and what you’d like to have happen instead
notes.meaning: 你观察到什么、工作受到什么影响、希望怎样改变
notes.explain: 按观察、影响、期望整理事实，避免把猜测动机或人格评价当成事实。
notes.example: I noticed the labels changed after handoff; it delayed the dashboard; I’d like us to agree on a change process.

notes.explain: 先说明自己的观察和影响，降低指责感；再提出邀请，而不是替对方定性。
notes.example: I noticed the change came after handoff. Would you have time to talk about it?

scenario.title: Repeated changes to shared issue labels
english: In the last three weekly handoffs, a colleague changed shared issue labels after you had finalized them.
You had to recheck duplicate items, which delayed the dashboard. You feel frustrated, but want to agree on a clear change process rather than blame your colleague.
The issue is recurring and affects work. First decide whether it merits a conversation; then draft a short, non-judgmental one-to-one invitation using “I” statements.
chinese: 最近三次每周交接中，同事都在你确认标签后更改共享问题标签。
你不得不重新核对重复事项，导致仪表盘延迟。你感到沮丧，但希望商定清楚的变更流程，而不是指责同事。
问题反复发生并影响工作。先判断是否值得谈，再用“I”陈述写一封简短、不评判的一对一沟通邀请。

firstAttempt.prompt: 先判断这件反复发生且已影响交付的事是否值得谈。然后用英文写三句以内的一对一邀请：客观说明观察到的行为、它对工作的影响，并询问是否可以讨论更好的做法。多用“I”表达，避免给同事贴标签。
firstAttempt.sample: I noticed the issue labels changed after I finalized the handoff in our last three weekly reviews. When that happens, I have to recheck duplicate items, which delays the dashboard. Would you have time this week to talk about agreeing on a label-change process before handoff?
firstAttempt.rationale: 这是反复发生且造成可说明的工作影响的问题，适合先与直接相关同事一对一谈。答案写出可观察行为、影响和希望讨论的改变，语气不指责。

words.meaning: 造成干扰的；影响正常工作的
words.example: The repeated changes were disruptive to the handoff.
words.translation: 反复的改动影响了交接。
words.note: 原文用来判断冲突是否已严重影响工作。

words.example: Start with an objective description of what happened.
words.translation: 先客观描述发生了什么。
words.note: 避免把对方的动机猜测写成事实。

words.example: Explain the impact on your work without blaming a colleague.
words.translation: 说明它对工作的影响，不要责怪同事。
words.note: 指出具体工作后果，让谈话聚焦问题。

words.example: Try a one-to-one conversation before involving anyone else.
words.translation: 先尝试一对一沟通，再考虑请其他人参与。
words.note: 原文建议先由直接相关的两方沟通。

words.example: I felt flustered when the discussion changed direction.
words.translation: 讨论突然转向时，我感到有些慌乱。
words.note: 可用来描述自己的感受，而非评价对方。

words.example: Use a non-judgmental tone when inviting a colleague to talk.
words.translation: 邀请同事谈话时，使用不带评判的语气。
words.note: 描述语气，不代表回避具体事实和影响。

structure.original: If you’re just a little annoyed, it might be best to let things slide, but if the conflict is truly disruptive, it probably warrants a 1:1 discussion.
analysis: If you’re just a little annoyed 是条件从句；it might be best to let things slide 表示一种可能的处理方式，might 保留判断空间。
but 引出对照情况：如果冲突确实影响工作，就可能值得一对一讨论。warrant 在此表示“使……有必要／值得”。
这句话先区分轻微不快与持续干扰工作的问题，再决定是否谈，不是鼓励把所有意见不合都升级。
structure.transfer: If repeated interruptions prevent you from sharing a safety concern, it may warrant a calm one-to-one conversation.

rewrite.bad: Your label changes keep wasting my time. Stop changing them after I finish.
rewrite.good: I noticed the issue labels changed after I finalized the handoff in our last three weekly reviews. When that happens, I have to recheck duplicate items, which delays the dashboard. Would you have time this week to talk about agreeing on a label-change process before handoff?
rewrite.translation: 我注意到最近三次每周交接中，我确认之后共享问题标签都发生了变化。这种情况让我不得不重新核对重复事项，导致仪表盘延迟。你这周有时间聊聊如何在交接前商定标签变更流程吗？
rewrite.pattern: I noticed [behavior]. When that happens, it affects [work]. Would you have time to talk about [desired change]?

cloze.prompt: I ___ the labels changed after I finalized the handoff.
cloze.why: I noticed 用可观察到的行为开场。

cloze.prompt: When that happens, it ___ the dashboard update.
cloze.why: 说明事件对工作的影响。

cloze.prompt: Would you have time to talk ___ the change process?
cloze.why: talk about 后接讨论主题。

dictation.text: Before you discuss, it’s good to pause and articulate your situation in an objective, honest way.
In your invite, see if you can acknowledge the conflict using more “I” statements than “you” statements.

translationPractice.prompt: 我注意到我确认交接后，问题标签被改了。
translationPractice.answer: I noticed the issue labels changed after I finalized the handoff.
translationPractice.why: I noticed 后先陈述可观察到的事情。

translationPractice.prompt: 这种情况发生时，会延误仪表盘更新。
translationPractice.answer: When that happens, it delays the dashboard update.
translationPractice.why: 用行为及影响的结构说明工作后果。

translationPractice.prompt: 你有时间谈谈标签变更流程吗？
translationPractice.answer: Would you have time to talk about a label-change process?
translationPractice.why: 用礼貌问句提出一对一讨论邀请。

choice.prompt: 同事连续三次在你确认交接后改标签，导致重复核对并延误仪表盘。哪种开场最适合邀请对方一对一沟通？
options: You keep changing labels and making everyone’s job harder. You need to stop.
I noticed the issue labels changed after I finalized the handoff. When that happens, I have to recheck duplicate items. Would you have time to talk about a label-change process?
It’s probably nothing, so I’ll just ask the manager to fix the labels for us.
choice.why: B 以可观察行为和工作影响为依据，并直接、非指责地邀请相关同事沟通。

output.prompt: 迁移情境：同事在最近两次设计评审中多次打断你，导致你没能说明发布风险。请用三句英文描述观察到的行为、对工作的影响，并邀请对方一对一讨论如何让每个人完成发言。
output.sample: I noticed I couldn’t finish my updates in our last two design reviews. When I lose my turn, the team doesn’t hear my release concerns. Would you have time this week to talk about making space for each update?
check: 是否描述具体可观察的行为，而非给同事贴标签？
是否说明这对工作或团队造成的影响？
是否用“I”表达提出一对一、非评判的沟通邀请？
